Matthew J. Bracken (born 1957) is an American author known for his controversial viewpoints and promotion of conspiracy theories related to government overreach and civil liberties. A former U.S. Navy SEAL, Bracken gained notoriety through his self-published novel series, including "Enemies Foreign and Domestic," which explores themes of governmental tyranny and the erosion of Second Amendment rights. His writings cater to audiences with libertarian and anti-government inclinations, often sparking debate and criticism.

=== Conspiracies and Controversies ===

Bracken has been a vocal proponent of numerous conspiracy theories, particularly those involving government surveillance and the alleged militarization against citizens. He frequently speaks at events and through online platforms, warning of perceived impending societal collapse and the dangers of potential governmental tyranny. Critics argue that his rhetoric can incite fear and division, while supporters laud him for championing personal freedom and self-reliance.

In addition to his literary work, Bracken has been involved in various public disputes over his outspoken conspiratorial views. He has appeared on several alternative media outlets where he further disseminates claims regarding government plots and deep state activities. These appearances often draw significant attention, both from supporters who share his views and from detractors who dismiss his assertions as unfounded and alarmist.

Bracken's controversial positions have also led to his involvement in several high-profile debates and discussions within the realm of conservative and libertarian circles. Despite the controversies, he maintains a dedicated following, particularly among those skeptical of mainstream narratives.
